frequency_question: How often have threatened or expected secondary sanctions against major foreign commercial banks for restricted energy trade been formally implemented with specific banking cutoffs?
membership_rule: Members are cases where U.S. secondary sanctions targeting major foreign commercial banks for energy trade were officially considered and faced a clear policy window. Excluded are primary sanctions, non-financial sanctions, and broad embargoes not targeting specific major commercial banks.

cases.name: Iran-Libya Sanctions Act implementation regarding European banks
CAATSA implementation regarding major non-Russian banks
Section 311 / PATRIOT Act secondary-style actions against foreign banks for North Korean/Iranian front activities

coverage_note: 3 named; covers the historical set of major secondary sanction frameworks applicable to systemically important commercial banks.
known_gaps: Waivers are frequently issued for major Chinese/foreign banks to avoid systemic macroeconomic fallout, creating a structural hurdle for full implementation.
skeleton: named cases of threatened major foreign bank financial cutoffs for sanctions evasion or prohibited trade, comparing broad state-level banking sanctions (typically waived or negotiated) versus smaller specific front-bank actions.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 3 major historical policy contexts where major commercial banks faced direct secondary sanction threats over strategic energy or major trade.
validity_reason: Relies on enduring institutional reluctance of the U.S. Treasury to cut off systemically important allied or adversary mega-banks due to global financial stability concerns, which remains stable across administrations.
